free_tier.stated: A 20 GB / 7-day trial: 'Get 20GB completely free – no credit card needed! Use it for 7 days or until you reach 20GB, whichever comes first.'

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap is published; no per-object cap is published; the unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, approximately 750 KB by convention, so 1 TiB of monthly transfer corresponds to roughly 1.4 million article fetches
per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: 3000+ days of binary and text retention, stated twice on the page

egress.terms: Unlimited downloads on every flat plan; speed and connections are tiered

interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563. No HTTP or object API exists for the download path, which is driven through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav.
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: A prepaid Abavia block stacks as fill under any primary and needs no renewal; the flats duplicate the XS News spool behind a lower speed ceiling.

limits_note: Flats and blocks are sold; the current vendor pages re-read state a 20 GB / 7-day free trial, 3000+ days of binary retention, unlimited downloads on flats, and the payment methods SEPA Direct Debit, Credit Card, iDeal, Sofort, Crypto, Bancontact, Belfius, Giropay and more. The earlier flat and block price ladder is no longer printed on the pages re-read today.
binding_note: On the flats the speed tier binds before any volume, because downloads are unlimited; on the blocks the byte allowance is the whole product and a 2 TB block is 24 months at 1 TiB/month.

identity_cost.detail: The trial asks for no credit card. Paid plans accept SEPA Direct Debit, Credit Card, iDeal, Sofort, Crypto, Bancontact, Belfius, Giropay and more.

reliability_note: Abavia reseller operated by Bulk News B.V. (Bulknews), AS48345 upstream. Cancellation needs at least 40 days' notice before renewal.
confidence_note: Every price is from the vendor page read on 2026-10-23. The free-trial claim is contradicted by the same page's price table and is documented as trial-only rather than free.
